description: This bar chart, from the paper "Breaking Bias, Building Bridges: Evaluation and Mitigation of Social Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis," illustrates the bias percentage for different contact conditions before and after intervention, categorized by two main experimental groups: "Extended Contact" and "Virtual Contact." The vertical axis represents "Bias Percentage" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 70, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis presents the two experimental conditions. Each condition is represented by a group of three stacked bars, corresponding to the three contact types: "No Contact," "Positive Contact," and "Negative Contact," as defined in the legend. The legend indicates that the "No Contact" category is shown in solid gray, "Positive Contact" in solid red, and "Negative Contact" in solid blue. The "Before" condition is represented by the solid-colored bars, while the "After" condition is represented by the hatched bars of the same color. For the "Extended Contact" group, the "No Contact Before" bar has a value of 39.50, the "Positive Contact Before" bar has a value of 31.83, and the "Negative Contact Before" bar has a value of 42.38. The "After" values for this group are 0.00, 0.00, and 47.28, respectively. For the "Virtual Contact" group, the "No Contact Before" bar has a value of 39.74, the "Positive Contact Before" bar has a value of 39.17, and the "Negative Contact Before" bar has a value of 43.83. The "After" values for this group are 10.00, 10.01, and 10.02, respectively. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the color and hatching used to distinguish the categories.
